At 1 day, the 90% CI of 282–297 is relatively tight, spanning about 15 units, because short-term dynamics are largely constrained by recent momentum and liquidity. By 1 week, the interval widens to 276–305, a 29-unit range, reflecting the possibility of meaningful news, sentiment shifts, or technical breakouts accumulating over several sessions. The widths are roughly consistent with a volatility-scaled diffusion process, where uncertainty grows approximately with the square root of time.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside my stated intervals include tail events such as unexpected central bank policy announcements, geopolitical shocks, or a sudden liquidity crisis that could produce sharp, discontinuous moves well beyond the 90% bounds. On the upside, a surprise positive catalyst — strong economic data, a major corporate announcement, or a short squeeze — could push the 1-month outcome above 322. On the downside, a risk-off episode, credit event, or sector-specific shock could drive the outcome below 262. My intervals are calibrated under relatively normal market conditions and implicitly assume no regime change, which is always a key vulnerability in probabilistic forecasting over multi-week horizons.

It is also worth noting that my 90% confidence intervals, by construction, are expected to miss the true outcome roughly 10% of the time. In practice, fat-tailed distributions in financial and economic data mean that extreme outcomes occur more frequently than Gaussian assumptions would suggest, so the true coverage of my stated intervals may be somewhat less than 90% in live conditions.
